{{Short description|German mathematician (born 1949)}}

[[File:Wolfgang Dahmen.jpg|thumb|Dahmen at [[Oberwolfach]], 2004]]
'''Wolfgang Dahmen''' (born 19 October 1949) is a German mathematician working in [[approximation theory]], [[numerical analysis]], and [[partial differential equations]]. In 2002, he was awarded the [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]] and in 2011 the [[Gauss Lectureship]]. He was also a [[taekwondo]] athlete. He has been the Chair of the [[Foundations of Computational Mathematics|Society for the Foundations of Computational Mathematics]] (2014–).

In 2019, he was named a [[SIAM Fellow]] "for contributions to numerical methods for partial differential equations, signal processing, and learning".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.siam.org/Prizes-Recognition/Fellows-Program/All-SIAM-Fellows/Class-of-2019|title=SIAM Fellows Class of 2019|accessdate=1 September 2019}}</ref> He was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Mathematical Society]], in the 2025 class of fellows.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/fellows_by_year.cgi?year=2025|title=2025 Class of Fellows of the AMS|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=2024-11-01}}</ref>
